title: Insight Tag
content:
# Insight Tag

Read, create and share a LinkedIn Insight Tag, manage its conversion rules, check when it last fired, and install it on Shopify or WordPress.

import { Tab, Tabs } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/tabs';

The LinkedIn Insight Tag is the site tag behind LinkedIn website conversions and retargeting.

## Read the tag

Zernio exposes it under the platform-neutral [tracking tags API](/guides/pixels) on your `linkedinads` connection.

With it you can:

- Read or create an ad account's tag
- Turn first-party tracking on or off
- Manage the conversion rules a page fires
- Share the tag with other ad accounts
- Install it on a connected [Shopify](/platforms/shopify/tracking-pixels) store or [WordPress](/platforms/wordpress/tracking-pixels) site

This page covers the site tag. A campaign's Dynamic UTM parameters are on [URL tracking tags](/platforms/linkedin-ads/url-tracking).

`GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/tracking-tags` lists one tag per active ad account on the connection.

`GET .../tracking-tags/{tagId}` adds:

- the base `code`
- `lastFiredTime`, the latest callback across the tag's domains (`null` when it never fired)
- `installed`
- the ad account's conversion rules as `events`

To create a tag, call `POST /v1/accounts/{accountId}/tracking-tags` with `adAccountId`. It is idempotent on LinkedIn: when the ad account already has an Insight Tag, it returns that tag instead of creating another.

`name` is required by the endpoint but ignored, because LinkedIn tags have no name.

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
import Zernio from '@zernio/node';

const zernio = new Zernio();

const { data } = await zernio.trackingtags.createTrackingTag({
  path: { accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d' },
  body: { adAccountId: '517258773', name: 'Insight Tag' }
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
from zernio import Zernio

client = Zernio()

data = client.tracking_tags.create_tracking_tag(
    account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    ad_account_id="517258773",
    name="Insight Tag",
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/accounts/66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d/tracking-tags" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "adAccountId": "517258773", "name": "Insight Tag" }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`201`):

```json
{
  "platform": "linkedinads",
  "tag": {
    "id": "9069513",
    "siteTagId": "9069513",
    "name": "Insight Tag 9069513",
    "platform": "linkedinads",
    "kind": "insight_tag",
    "status": "active",
    "ownerAdAccountId": "517258773",
    "code": "<script type=\"text/javascript\">\n_linkedin_partner_id = \"9069513\";...</script>",
    "lastFiredTime": 1804150800,
    "installed": true,
    "events": [
      { "id": "30828442", "name": "Purchase", "type": "PURCHASE", "status": "active", "siteEvent": "purchase", "siteEventId": "30828442", "defaultValue": 50, "currency": "USD", "clickWindowDays": 30, "viewWindowDays": 7 }
    ]
  }
}
```

`PATCH .../tracking-tags/{tagId}` accepts only `firstPartyCookieStatus`. It maps to LinkedIn's first-party tracking switch: `first_party_cookie_enabled` or `first_party_cookie_disabled`.

`empty` answers `400`, because the switch has no unset state.

## Ids

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| `accountId` | The `linkedinads` connection |
| `tagId` | The Insight Tag's partner id (numeric). The API id is the id the site embeds, so `siteTagId` equals `id`. |
| `adAccountId` | A LinkedIn ad account id, numeric or `urn:li:sponsoredAccount:<id>`. Conversion rules and domains live under an ad account; per-tag calls default to the account that owns the tag. |
| `events[].id` | The conversion rule id. For rules a page can fire, `siteEventId` is the same id (the `conversionId` a page sends). |

`kind` is `insight_tag`. An ad account holds at most one Insight Tag.

The tag has no name of its own, so Zernio returns `Insight Tag <id>`.

## Conversion rules

LinkedIn conversions are separate rules owned by an ad account. Zernio exposes them as the tag's events on `/tracking-tags/{tagId}/events`.

Pass `adAccountId` when the rules you want are not on the account that owns the tag.

| Operation | Behavior |
|-----------|----------|
| List | Every conversion rule of the ad account, enabled or not (`status` `active` or `inactive`). |
| Create | Creates an event-specific Insight Tag rule, the kind a page fires by id. Not idempotent. |
| Update | Partial update of any field below. |
| Delete | Disables the rule (`state: "disabled"`); `PATCH` with `enabled: true` turns it back on. LinkedIn has no delete for rules (`DELETE /rest/conversions/{id}` has no route). |

The body takes:

- `name`
- a LinkedIn conversion type in `type` (`PURCHASE`, `ADD_TO_CART`, `LEAD`, `SIGN_UP`, `KEY_PAGE_VIEW`, ...) or a `siteEvent`
- `enabled`
- `defaultValue` with `currency`, both together, in the ad account's currency. The event's own value wins when it carries one.
- `clickWindowDays` and `viewWindowDays`

<Tabs items={['Node.js', 'Python', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```typescript
const { data } = await zernio.trackingtags.createTrackingTagEvent({
  path: { accountId: '66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d', tagId: '9069513' },
  body: { name: 'Purchase', siteEvent: 'purchase', defaultValue: 50, currency: 'USD', clickWindowDays: 30, viewWindowDays: 7 }
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
data = client.tracking_tags.create_tracking_tag_event(
    account_id="66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d",
    tag_id="9069513",
    name="Purchase",
    site_event="purchase",
    default_value=50,
    currency="USD",
    click_window_days=30,
    view_window_days=7,
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/accounts/66b2e19d8c3f5a7e9d0b1c2d/tracking-tags/9069513/events" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "name": "Purchase", "siteEvent": "purchase", "defaultValue": 50, "currency": "USD", "clickWindowDays": 30, "viewWindowDays": 7 }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Response (`201`):

```json
{
  "platform": "linkedinads",
  "event": { "id": "30828442", "name": "Purchase", "type": "PURCHASE", "status": "active", "siteEvent": "purchase", "siteEventId": "30828442", "defaultValue": 50, "currency": "USD", "clickWindowDays": 30, "viewWindowDays": 7 }
}
```

Rules for the [Conversions API](/platforms/linkedin-ads/conversions) and URL-match rules cannot be fired by id from a page. They carry no `siteEventId` or `siteEvent`.

**`page_view`** maps to `KEY_PAGE_VIEW` on create, but the Shopify install never fires it. The base tag already reports every page, and a key-page-view rule on every page would count each visit as a conversion.

## Share with other ad accounts

`GET`, `POST` and `DELETE .../tracking-tags/{tagId}/shared-accounts` list, grant and revoke other ad accounts' access to the tag. Call them from the ad account that owns it.

A grant gives `USE_ONLY` access. The recipient can use the tag and its conversions but cannot edit, share or unshare it.

`sharedAccounts[]` covers the ad accounts this connection can see, with each account's role in its `name`.

**One tag per account.** LinkedIn allows one Insight Tag per ad account. A grant to an account that already uses another tag answers `400` (LinkedIn itself returns a bare `500` there).

**Last account.** Revoking the last ad account on a tag also answers `400`. LinkedIn would accept it and leave the tag orphaned, so share it with another account first.

## Stats

LinkedIn exposes no fire counts, so `GET .../tracking-tags/{tagId}/stats` is a health check. It returns two kinds of row:

- One per domain the tag has fired on: `kind: "domain"`, `domainName`, `lastFiredTime`, `creationTime`, `blocked`
- One per conversion rule: `kind: "conversion_rule"`, `id`, `name`, `type`, `conversionMethod`, `status`, `lastFiredTime`

## Install on a store

**Shopify.** Every page view goes to `px.ads.linkedin.com/collect`. That is LinkedIn's documented image pixel, with the parameter names `insight.min.js` sends.

Any other storefront event is sent only when the ad account has an enabled, page-fireable rule of the matching type. The most recently fired one wins.

That event goes as a `conversionId` hit with the value, currency, order id and an `eventId`. LinkedIn uses the `eventId` to deduplicate against the Conversions API.

The `li_fat_id` click id is captured from the landing URL. See [the event mapping](/platforms/shopify/tracking-pixels#event-mapping).

**WordPress.** The install adds LinkedIn's Insight Tag base code. LinkedIn has no official WordPress plugin, so a blocked install points to pasting the tag's `code` into the theme.

<Callout type="warn">The Shopify install stores the rule ids it found. Install again after you add or change conversion rules.</Callout>

## What the API cannot do

| Operation | Evidence |
|-----------|----------|
| Delete an Insight Tag | Absent from LinkedIn's docs; `DELETE /rest/insightTags/{id}` has no route. |
| Delete a conversion rule | Absent from the conversion-tracking docs; `DELETE /rest/conversions/{id}` answers `404` "No virtual resource found", so delete disables. |
| Name or rename the tag | Insight Tags have no name field. |
| Fire counts | LinkedIn reports last-callback times only. |

## If it fails

| Error | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `400` on `firstPartyCookieStatus` | The value is `empty`, and the switch has no unset state | Send `first_party_cookie_enabled` or `first_party_cookie_disabled` |
| `400` on a share grant | The ad account already uses another Insight Tag, and LinkedIn allows one per account | Revoke the account's current tag first, then grant again |
| `400` on a share revoke | It is the last ad account on the tag, which would leave it orphaned | Share the tag with another account first |
| A page never fires a rule | Conversions API and URL-match rules cannot be fired by id from a page | Create an Insight Tag rule on `/events` |
| Shopify fires the old rules | The install stores the rule ids it found | Install again after you add or change rules |
